upstream_anchor: RulePropagateCopy (ruleaction.cc:3943), the marker arm and its own addrforce refusal
hypothesis_status: NONE ON FILE; the round-5 refutation's two readings were decided by p-code, in favour of (a)
filed_hypothesis: none offered (refuter verdict: INCONCLUSIVE -- (a) the store is deleted and the surviving register def prints, or (b) the store survives and its output merges into the wrong HighVariable)
decisions: READING (a), DECIDED BY P-CODE, NOT BY ARGUMENT. `print raw` after `decompile` on the witness shows the loop header as `s0x...f73c(0x140003606) = MULTIEQUAL(s0x...f73c(0x1400035e9), EAX(0x1400035fd))` with `EAX(0x1400035fd) = s0x...f73c(0x140003606) + 1`. There is no COPY left at 0x1400035ff: the store IS deleted, and RulePropagateCopy is what deleted it. That puts the fix in P3, not in P6 merge/naming, which is the fork the refuter asked the builder to decide first.

THE REGISTER CLAUSE IS LOAD-BEARING AND WAS BOUGHT BY A RED GATE. The first predicate (same-address MULTIEQUAL + value computed from the phi output) regressed the upstream datatest `forloop_loaditer` from `for (loopvar = ptr; ...; loopvar = loopvar[3])` to a `while` with the iterator statement demoted into the body -- 1/675. The cause is that `add dword [rbp-4],1` has the same shape with a SLEIGH `unique` as the intermediate, and keeping that store alive displaces the loop's iterator statement. A unique never becomes a named variable and its store is always folded by Merge, so restricting the brake to a register intermediate is what separates the two, and it restores 675/675.

THE COPY-CHAIN WALK IS NOT COSMETIC. On the witness the counter's load side is already folded when the write-back is considered, so the increment reads the phi output directly; on a gcc -O0 ELF the rule pool reaches the other propagation first and the increment reads a register COPY of it. A predicate written against a direct reference fires or does not depending on which propagation the pool got to first. `resolves_to` walks COPYs to depth 4.

THE FILED TITLE IS HALF RIGHT. The store is gone, but an assignment IS emitted -- attributed to the register's HighVariable. The refuter's observation that `v7` is declared bare `int v7;` with no storage comment while every other register local carries one (`unsigned int v10; // eax`) is what that looks like from the printer.

TIEDSTOREKEEP (DIV-105) IS NOT THE FIX AND THE REFUTER'S A/B STANDS. Its predicate requires the stored value to come from a CALL/CALLIND/CALLOTHER/INDIRECT; a counter bump is an INT_ADD, so it declines here and flipping it either way leaves the loops byte-identical. The two brakes are separate options for that reason: same rule, same op, different shapes, independently ablatable.

A PRINTER HALF WAS NECESSARY, AND THE SWEEP IS WHAT FOUND IT. Where Merge would have succeeded anyway the kept COPY becomes the statement's root op with the arithmetic implied beneath it, and `PrintC::emitInplaceOp` matches only a bare two-input op -- 85 statements across 20 binaries fell back from `v += 1` to `v = v + 1` (correct C, and exactly upstream's form, but a silent loss of DIV-36's sugar in loops that were never broken). `inplace_through_copy` renders from the inner op when the COPY's input is IMPLIED; an explicit input is left alone because there the statement really is `out = <that name>`. That takes the `+=` regressions from 58 to 9 and the total normalized corpus delta from 365/339 lines to 296/270.

THE `high_is_input` READING OF THE MERGE DECLINE IS WRONG. `Merge::merge_test_required` refuses to merge an input high into an address-tied output, which looked like the explanation for why five loops decline in one function. Requiring a function-input varnode at the register's storage was implemented and measured: it removed the collateral AND un-fixed all five witness loops. Whatever declines the merge here, it is not that.

NO STAGES TESTCASE AND NO PROMOTED CLI PROBE, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. The propagation reproduces easily; the MISPRINT needs Merge to decline, and no synthetic does. Five fixtures were built and measured -- gcc -O0 C with 3 and with 5 loops, hand-written x86-64 assembly with the MSVC `mov/inc/mov` counter shape (the brake fires 7 times per counter and the C is identical either way), the same with typed libc call returns stored to locals, and the same with the register made a function input -- plus the isolated loop region of the witness itself via `--define-function`, which repairs. DIV-105 records the same negative for the same function and the same Merge gate. The need's acceptance target is `binary_source: dataset` and CI has no dataset, so `verify --promote` cannot vendor it; the acceptance is measured PASS on the dataset image instead.
acceptance: PASS -- scripts.repipe.verify --need live-loop-counter-stores: total 1, pass 1, closed 1, regressed 0
sweep_method: `kuna decompile-all` in both arms (default vs `--option loopcounterstore off`) over the 134-binary arena crackme corpus, compared per binary; three binaries whose 240 s wall-clock timeout landed in one arm only, and one whose 10 s per-function decompile budget did, are excluded as timing artifacts
sweep_changed_detail: 13 of 130 binaries differ, 296 removed / 270 added lines after normalizing variable numbering (3544/5441 raw, the rest is renumbering cascade). The named categories: the 5 repaired witness loops; 9 `bool vN; // cf` flag temporaries that stop being emitted, with `v8 = v10 == 0; ... if (v8)` becoming `if (!v9)`; 22 sites where two statements fuse (`V = V != N` plus `V = V + V` becomes `V = V + (V != N)`); net +9 `for` loops recovered where a `while` with a comma-initialiser becomes a real `for` header (`while (v = a + -0x10, 0 <= v)` -> `for (v = a + -0x10; 0 <= v; v = v + -0x10)`); and the one named cost, net +5 conditions that gain a comma-separated copy (`while (*(char *)(a1 + v5))` -> `while (v5 = v3, *(char *)(a1 + v5))`), where the surviving copy is hoisted into the loop condition.
speed_method: scripts.pipeline.timeit, median of 7, ObfuscationFiesta.exe sub_140002530, twice on a machine concurrently running the sweep and the workspace suite
speed_note: both runs measured faster with the brake ON (-16.19% and -30.53%), which is not a claimed speedup: the host was loaded and returncopysplit's record puts the single-target noise floor at +/-20%. The claim is only that no slowdown is measurable; the brake is one extra predicate on a path RulePropagateCopy already walks.
